title: Scientists uncover ‘very detailed map’ of an enzyme target for rare metabolic disease | Fierce Biotech
summary:
For some rare genetic diseases, the problem isn't a missing protein but the buildup of toxic molecules that the body can no longer clear away.

In a recent study published in Science Advances, a group of researchers from Mount Sinai identified the crystal structure of an upstream enzyme in a rare genetic disease, glutaric aciduria type 1 (GA1). title: The Medicine Maker | CAR T Therapy Shows Early Promise in Stiff Person Syndrome
summary:
A single infusion of an investigational CAR T-cell therapy has produced significant improvements in mobility and disability among patients with stiff person syndrome (SPS), according to a phase 2 clinical trial published in JAMA Neurology. The findings offer further evidence that CAR T-cell therapies could provide lasting benefits beyond oncology, potentially transforming treatment for difficult-to-manage autoimmune diseases.

title: Developer finishes FDA application for Friedreich's ataxia treatment
summary:
Larimar Therapeutics has completed an application asking the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to approve nomlabofusp, its experimental protein replacement therapy for Friedreich’s ataxia (FA).

Because nomlabofusp had previously earned certain regulatory designations aimed at speeding its development, Larimar was allowed to do a rolling application – meaning the company could submit sections of the application as soon as they were ready, rather than waiting for the whole thing to be done.
